findings.body:
Line 3 now iterates only `parts.iter().enumerate().take(parts.len().saturating_sub(1))`, which yields indices 0..len-2. The loop body appends each yielded part, so the final element is never pushed. For ["a","b","c"] the output is "a,b", and for ["a"] or [] the loop body never runs, so the output is "".

Trigger: Calling join with any slice of length 1 or more, for example join(&["a","b","c"]).]

Impact: Every caller of the public `join` function gets a string missing its last element for any non-empty input. A single-element input returns an empty string. Any caller that relies on the result is silently affected, and no error is raised.
findings.suggestion: Iterate over `parts.iter().enumerate()` without the `take(...)` adapter, so that every part is appended and separators are placed before parts with i > 0.
